articles.title_orig: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.
Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.
The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.
Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.
Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.
The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.
Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.
Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.
The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".
It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".
Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.
The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.
On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.
Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it said.
Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title_orig: Zelenskiy confirms Ukraine hit Russian ship in Gulf of Finland, ally Norway urges caution
articles.title_zh: Zelenskiy confirms Ukraine hit Russian ship in Gulf of Finland, ally Norway urges caution
articles.content_orig:
A Russian cargo ship struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland has left Finnish territorial waters after posing a “serious danger” there, according to Finland’s President Alexander Stubb.
Stubb said late on Sunday that Finland would continue working to maintain stability and security in the Gulf of Finland and thanked the authorities for their response to Saturday’s incident.
Finland’s military said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters, where it was previously anchored. The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship.
A fire aboard the Sparta II continued to burn through the night despite efforts to extinguish it, the Finnish coastguard said.
“Unfortunately, the consequences of Russia’s war of aggression are also visible in our region,” Stubb said on X.
Pictures and video released by the coastguard on Sunday showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannon overnight to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck.
Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia’s northwestern coastal region of Leningrad this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling onto NATO territory.
The ship, bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, the Finnish Defence Forces said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.
Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo suggested the incident was related to Russia’s war on Ukraine.
“War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity … Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor,” Orpo said on X.
The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday.
Finland’s military said last week that it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.
The Sparta II is a 121-metre (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to data from the London Stock Exchange.
The vessel is subject to United States sanctions, according to the US Department of the Treasury.
Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Ministry of Defence, according to the company’s website.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27 adds new Messages app setting I instantly started using
articles.title_zh: iOS 27 adds new Messages app setting I instantly started using
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27 brought several new features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.
With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.
Siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a big upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar , Mail , and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.
In Messages, there’s a new setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.
The audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.
Since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of users have encountered— including Justin Bieber —it’s very easy to hit by accident.
Thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:
Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’
If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.
Will you disable the audio button in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

Ryan got his start in journalism as an Editor at MacStories, where he worked for four years covering Apple news, writing app reviews, and more. For two years he co-hosted the Adapt podcast on Relay FM, which focused entirely on the iPad. As a result, it should come as no surprise that his favorite Apple device is the iPad Pro.

articles.title_orig: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.title_zh: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.content_orig:
Gisèle Pelicot, the French woman who spoke out about being drugged and raped by her husband and dozens of other men, said Monday that she had been "once again humiliated" after nude photos and videos of her were sent to media outlets to promote a book that she said is dismissive of her husband's crimes.
Pelicot, 73, told France's BFMTV that she will take legal action against the publisher, Tinard, and the author of the book, French psychoanalyst Sabine Prokhoris.
The book criticizes the concept of coercive control and questions whether Pelicot was really a victim, suggesting she could have been complicit in her husband's actions despite her having been surreptitiously drugged for years.
"I am deeply shocked that images relating to my most intimate life could be exhibited and exploited for commercial purposes," Pelicot said in a statement to the French broadcaster, adding: "Above all, I refuse to have my story rewritten by implying that I was complicit in what I suffered."
"Today, I find myself humiliated, exposed, and hurt once again. As if the ordeal of the trial wasn't enough," she said. "I fought to regain my dignity and my freedom. I will not let anyone take them away from me."
Pelicot became a global symbol of resilience in 2024 when she waived her right to anonymity in her then-husband Dominique's trial. He was convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison for his abuse — and for inviting 50 other men to join him in raping his wife while she was incapacitated repeatedly over the course of a decade.
"How can you imagine that your husband is drugging you? It's unthinkable — impossible," she told CBS News in February. "In fact, I was manipulated for about 10 years. Because he was looking me in the eyes every day while knowing he was poisoning me. But I never saw that. I saw a kind, caring man."
She said she waived her anonymity during the trial to show that "shame has to change sides," from victims to perpetrators.
On its website, the publisher Tinard said it had offered "our sincerest apologies" to Pelicot and that it would not be reprinting the book after 280 copies already printed are sold. It said "no images of rape or pornographic videos were leaked to the press."
It is not clear where the publisher got the nude images of Pelicot. In her statements to French media, Pelicot did not question their authenticity. She also did not confirm or deny a report by the French weekly news outlet Le Canard Enchaîne, which said the images were among those taken by her former husband and presented during his trial as evidence.
Prokhoris, the author, said she had given "full responsibility" for the promotional campaign to the publisher, according to French news agency AFP.
AFP said the back-cover blurb on the book asks readers to "think freely" about the notion of coercive control, which Prokhoris describes as "a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy" that is "fundamentally ambiguous" and, she says, involves "each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way."
"There are two types of violence that have been committed," Pelicot's lawyer Christophe Bigot told BFM. "There is, on the one hand, the fact that intimate images of her were sent without her consent in the context of purely commercial communication, and then there is a book that calls into question her status as a victim."
"It is a clear violation of the law, and she does not intend to let it go unchallenged," he said.

articles.title_orig: US lawmakers vow to investigate Jensen Huang and Trump over Nvidia scandal
articles.title_zh: US lawmakers vow to investigate Jensen Huang and Trump over Nvidia scandal
articles.content_orig:
Republicans have broken ranks with Donald Trump for his efforts to help reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive.
Members of the US president’s party expressed their anger after Mr Trump boasted about vouching for the 63-year-old, who had admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and has been accused of other affairs.
The Trump administration has tried to alleviate fears of Chinese interference, with some officials questioning whether Alice Huang, the suspected spy , was sharing top-secret intelligence.
Rejecting administration assurances that national security concerns were resolved, Republicans demanded answers, in a rare instance of threatening to use their oversight power against the president.
“Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior US officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk,” John Curtis, Utah’s Republican senator, said on social media.
“I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?”
Tom Cotton, Arkansas’s Republican senator and the chairman of the intelligence committee, said Congress should move quickly on legislation to closely monitor the export of advanced chips used to train and run AI – a market dominated by Nvidia.
“I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access,” Mr Cotton wrote on X.
“Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”
The reinstatement was a shocking reversal for Mr Huang, coming just 11 days after he was forced out over claims he had three extramarital affairs, most notably one with Ms Huang, the alleged Chinese spy. Megaspeed , Ms Huang’s data centre, is under justice department investigation for allegations of smuggling AI chips to China.
Mr Trump defended Mr Huang, boasting that he was the one who “convinced” the board to bring the chief executive back.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” he told CNBC. “And I convinced them… I made the deal.”
Pete Ricketts, Nebraska’s Republican senator, criticised the move, saying Mr Huang’s “behaviour does not support reinstatement” and citing the tech board’s concerns that its chief executive lacked “candour”.
Mr Ricketts said that Nvidia’s decision did not pardon Mr Huang from testifying before Congress, adding that he “look[ed] forward” to investigating his behaviour before the Senate in December.
“Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress,” Mr Ricketts wrote. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips.”
Mr Cotton said the furore surrounding Nvidia and Megaspeed was “just the tip of the iceberg”, adding: “It’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back.”
Questions have been raised about why Mr Trump ignored the scandal and lobbied so aggressively for Mr Huang’s return. Recently published findings point to money as the main motive .
Since being sworn in at the start of 2025, the US president has bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 108 times, with trading reaching up to $98m (£75m).
Mr Trump, who claims these decisions were made by independent advisers, carried out 751 trades in September alone, according to the filings.
Earlier disclosures included a sale of between $500,001 and $1m of Nvidia shares on May 18, just a few days after Mr Trump returned from a state visit to China – with Mr Huang joining the president on Air Force One.
The New York Times reported that before Mr Huang boarded the presidential jet, Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, briefed Mr Trump on intelligence about the chief executive’s possible relationship with a suspected spy.
Mr Trump denied the briefing and questioned whether Ms Huang was a mole.
US officials said that Ms Huang was in contact with officials from China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out the affair.
However, there was no smoking-gun intelligence to prove that she was collecting information on Mr Huang or sharing it with Beijing, according to sources who spoke to The Wall Street Journal.
Some US officials said the links between Ms Huang and China’s spy agency were circumstantial, while others said that her contact alone with such officials posed a risk to national security.
When announcing Mr Huang’s return, Nvidia said its board had “received input from senior levels of the United States government”, leading it to conclude that the “reinstatement poses no national security risk”.
John Cornyn, Texas’s Republican senator, criticised the assertion. “No national security risk?” he posted on social media. “Based on what?”
On Tuesday, it became clear that Mr Trump had profited from Mr Huang’s return.
Nvidia stock soared more than 30 per cent on Monday, adding nearly $1tn (£766bn) in value to the company and putting Mr Trump in line for personal gains of up to $15m (£11.5m), the Financial Times reported.

articles.title_orig: Where To Find Lucia’s Best Hairstyle In ‘GTA 6’
articles.title_zh: Where To Find Lucia’s Best Hairstyle In ‘GTA 6’
articles.content_orig:
To change your clothes and appearance quickly in Grand Theft Auto 6 , you must prep a spare outfit and keep a few accessories on hand. Whether you want to become anonymous or dress to impress, you'll be changing your look quite often, so it's handy to know the best ways to change your outfit.
Here's how to swap outfits, hairstyles, and accessories in GTA 6 .
In GTA 6 , you can swap between any clothes you own using your wardrobe (in your home) or a changing room at any gym or clothing store. You heard that right; realism makes way for convenience, allowing you to freely change into any of your clothes without having to purchase new ones (though you can still do so if you like).
To find a clothing store or gym , open the map and look for pink T-shirt and blue weight icons, respectively. If you'd like to buy new clothes for fun, open the map, scroll to "style," and select the style you're looking for to find every matching store (such as "sportswear" or "formal"). The changing rooms are usually at the back, but if you're looking to browse clothes, interact with the racks.
To change clothes on the run , you can store up to 10 sets of clothes (five per character) in your car trunk. The important thing is to add these outfits to your trunk at any wardrobe or changing room – before you go robbing banks and such.
Don't worry if you're stuck in the middle of nowhere without a vehicle; to change clothes quickly, even if the police are looking for you and know your current outfit, you can use the Scooter Bros app to have your vehicle delivered to your current location. Once you've added an outfit to your trunk, you can grab it from any car you own. Just beware that the vehicle delivery service may cost a few hundred dollars depending on the distance and the vehicle's damage, so don't use it too often.
To change clothes in your car, go to "loadout," "items," and select one of your saved outfits at the bottom right.
If you simply wish to change your appearance because the police are chasing you, and you need to become anonymous , you should equip some sunglasses and a hat . If you were already wearing them while committing a crime, take them off instead. To do so, open the item wheel to select the eyewear on the left and headwear on the right, and toggle them on or off. If you don't have any glasses or hats, buy them at a store, loot them from an enemy, or rob a civilian.
If you already know you're about to commit a crime, you can also change your appearance by putting on a mask and taking it off later – best to avoid the opposite (committing a crime without a mask, then equipping one after), as this might make you suspicious.
You can change your appearance in GTA 6 more drastically by getting a new hairstyle, a tattoo, or makeup. While a new hairstyle can also help you evade the cops, visiting a store takes more time than putting on a hat and glasses, so these types of appearance changes are more fun than practical. To find new hair and makeup styles, open the map, scroll to "style" in the legend, and click either "hair and beauty" or "tattoos." The hair salons aren't gendered, and you can also use them to change Lucia's makeup or Jason's facial hair. To find the style you're looking for, check the salon's description.
If you're just getting started in GTA 6 , we have plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first , recommendations for the best ways to make money fast , and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.
Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy , too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6 's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission , and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes . You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

articles.title_orig: Snowden on steroids: AI agents in phones trigger surveillance fears
articles.title_zh: Snowden on steroids: AI agents in phones trigger surveillance fears
articles.content_orig:
AI agents are lurking in your phone, hoovering up your messages, pictures and emails in a privacy breach that "makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," privacy proponents are warning.
Privacy-preserving messaging app Signal has started blocking screenshots by default in an attempt to stop AI agents from reading people's screens and capturing potentially sensitive data.
The makers behind Signal — which is considered the industry gold standard for confidential, encrypted messaging — warned that Google, Apple and Microsoft are integrating autonomous agents "deep" within their device operating systems, allowing the agents to bypass privacy safeguards in individual apps.
"The ability for billions of devices to permanently spy on their users makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," Udbhav Tiwari, head of strategy and global affairs at Signal, told POLITICO, referring to the 2013 disclosures about mass U.S. government surveillance.
Tiwari warned that governments with a penchant for surveillance could ask tech firms for access to data gathered by AI agents, skipping the need to break end-to-end encryption or install malware on someone’s device.
Apple, Google and Microsoft declined to comment on Signal’s claims.
Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal, policy adviser at European digital rights group EDRi, called for "serious limits" on what AI agents can access. "There is something deeply worrying about a not-so-far-away future where the companies controlling our operating systems can effectively decide how much privacy we are allowed to have, even when we deliberately choose services designed to protect it," she said.
"Probably the most sensitive device in your entire life is your phone. If it gets nicked, the person stealing your phone is not going to have access to your whole life. We're undoing all those safeguards by inviting AI agents onto these devices," said Gus Hosein, executive director of privacy NGO Privacy International.
Signal is pushing for makers of operating systems to provide tools so apps can opt out of AI data access and processing.
Operating system level AI agents have already launched in many countries globally, but rollout is slower in the EU. Apple has cited the EU’s digital competition rulebook as a key hurdle for the rollout of its latest AI virtual assistant features.
Social media giant Meta is also rolling out its own AI agent, Muse, which launched in the United Kingdom on Tuesday . Digital regulators including the Information Commissioner's Office already warned last month that AI agent products “may amplify and accelerate risks” to consumers. The British privacy authority said this week that Meta committed to a “voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme” to enable ongoing scrutiny, and that it is preparing new guidance on how privacy law applies to AI agents.
Meta has said its new AI agent is “private, safe and secure by design," and that it has "engaged constructively" with regulators.
Beyond the most high-risk situations, there are concerns AI agents could also gather data to repurpose for things like AI training or targeted advertising.
Ireland’s powerful privacy regulator, which oversees data protection policies at Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft and other tech giants, is also cracking down on how "third-party" data is hoovered up by AI agents and repurposed.
Third-party data pertains to someone who isn't directly dealing with the AI agent; for example, you send a message or holiday pictures to a friend without knowing they've given an AI agent permission to access their messages.
The Irish Data Protection Commission intervened in the past month to stop Elon Musk-owned X from feeding AI models with third party data collected by its Grok Bot, POLITICO first reported .
Irish Data Protection Commissioner Niamh Sweeney said last week that it is "much more challenging" to inform third parties about their data being processed, or give them a chance to opt out, when they have “no idea” that their data could also be scooped up.

articles.title_orig: Why Amazon’s Rival to Starlink Is Struggling to Catch Up With SpaceX
articles.title_zh: Why Amazon’s Rival to Starlink Is Struggling to Catch Up With SpaceX
articles.content_orig:
A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket .
The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.
The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon said, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight.
Amazon cast a wide net when it started signing deals for launch services five years ago, securing rides on 108 flights with every available medium- or heavy-lift rocket in the West to place a fleet of 3,232 satellites into low-Earth orbit. As of Tuesday, Amazon and its launch partners have completed 17 of those flights, with one mission failure.
Amazon executives initially bought up capacity from US-based United Launch Alliance, Europe’s Arianespace, and Blue Origin. Nearly all of those launch contracts depended on rockets still in development: ULA’s Vulcan, Europe’s Ariane 6, and Blue Origin’s New Glenn.
Each launch vehicle faced development delays, as all new rockets do. New Glenn has been grounded since May after an explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in Florida. ULA’s Vulcan will be sidelined for months after misfiring during a mission with Amazon satellites on November 15.
Amazon started booking launches in 2023 with SpaceX. Falcon 9 successfully launched Amazon’s first three missions last year, each with 24 satellites. Amazon soon reserved 10 more flights on SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket as delays mounted with Amazon Leo’s other launch providers, especially ULA and Blue Origin.
The relationship between Amazon and SpaceX is a peculiar one. Amazon aims to catch up to SpaceX’s Starlink network, now boasting more than 11,000 satellites, to bring competition to the satellite broadband market. Federal regulators approved Amazon Leo’s second-generation constellation earlier this year, an addition that will bring the fleet to more than 7,000 satellites in the 2030s. Amazon also plans a direct-to-device service, joining SpaceX and others in the pursuit of consumer demand for mobile connectivity.
But Starlink is far ahead. SpaceX has repurposed the Starlink satellite design for use on several US military programs, and Starlink launches on Falcon 9 are winding down as SpaceX’s Starship enters service . Starship is capable of launching heavier, more powerful Starlink satellites, a culmination that will only widen the gap with Amazon and other competitors in the satellite Internet business.
Starlink’s move to Starship opens up launch slots on Falcon 9, allowing Amazon to accelerate its launches with SpaceX in the near term. But SpaceX doesn’t plan to keep Falcon 9 around for long. The company has reportedly stopped accepting commercial Falcon 9 bookings after 2028.
That means Amazon Leo needs its other launch providers to step up. Arianespace is doing so, with four successful Ariane 6 flights for Amazon this year. Amazon reserved six additional flights with Arianespace in September as Ariane 6 proved its mettle.
But there are questions about Europe’s ability to ramp up production of Ariane 6 rockets, which are single-use and not reusable like Falcon 9 and New Glenn. Europe’s rocket factories are sized to support a launch cadence of up to nine or 10 Ariane 6 flights per year. Arianespace will likely reach six Ariane 6 flights this year, with one more remaining before the end of December.
European taxpayers paid for development of the Ariane 6 and the industrial capacity to build the rockets, and they continue to subsidize each Ariane 6 flight, whether it carries a European government payload or commercial satellites for a large American corporation like Amazon.
European government ministers are mulling proposals to increase Ariane 6 production to meet surging demand from commercial users and Europe’s internal space programs. A decision could come next month , but a ramp-up in launch cadence won’t happen overnight.
Amazon paid United Launch Alliance hundreds of millions of dollars for expansion at Cape Canaveral, Florida, to prepare for as many as 25 Vulcan launches per year. Such a launch cadence is a long way off for ULA, which has now launched Vulcan five times (with one failure) in its three years of service.
Blue Origin, owned by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, could resume New Glenn flights early next year after completing a launch pad rebuild. It is not clear when Amazon might begin launching on New Glenn, but finding slots in the rocket’s launch schedule could be difficult as Blue Origin prioritizes work for NASA’s Artemis lunar program.
In the meantime, SpaceX will offer Amazon its most assured rides to space. Falcon 9s can launch from Cape Canaveral every few days, and Amazon is ready to tap into that capability with hundreds of satellites in storage waiting to go to orbit.

articles.title_orig: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station
articles.title_zh: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
China has announced the crew for the upcoming space launch to its Tiangong space station , including a Pakistani astronaut, who will be the first foreigner to board the orbiting outpost.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who served as a pilot in the Pakistan Air Force, will board China’s Shenzhou 24 spacecraft powered by the Long March 2F rocket along with Chinese colleagues Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Tuesday.
The trio is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China at 8.18am local time on Wednesday, the agency said.
Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed launch and marks the first joint space flight mission conducted by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of Beijing’s crewed space mission programme .
Mr Ali, 40, would spend about a week aboard the Chinese space station as a payload specialist and return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with crew members Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying, returning after their six-month rotation.
“I’m not flying for myself; I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hope of 250 million Pakistanis,” he told reporters at a press briefing on Tuesday.
The Pakistani astronaut hoped space cooperation between the two Asian countries would go from one astronaut in one flight to multiple joint missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond.
Mr Ali has trained for seven months since he was selected in April, including learning Mandarin for better communication with his crewmates.
“The labels and operating instructions aboard the spacecraft and space station are all in Chinese, and the Pakistani astronaut began training with virtually no foundation in the language," Mr Hongbo said.
On board the space station, Mr Ali would conduct scientific projects in the fields of biotechnology and materials, as well as an in-orbit experiment on photosynthetic microorganisms, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported.
“To every child who’s watching while I’m in orbit, look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams,” he said.
All facilities and equipment are in good condition for Wednesday’s launch, CMSA said.
The three-module Tiangong space station was completed in late 2022, and ever since, rotating six-month-long missions have kept the orbiting outpost constantly crewed ever since.
China hopes. to double the size of the space station in coming years, and facilitate more joint missions with crews from other countries.
This comes as the US and China are locked in a space race to the Moon, with both countries aiming to land boots on the lunar surface by 2030.

articles.title_orig: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.title_zh: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.content_orig:
China’s anticorruption watchdog has launched an investigation into the top Chinese Communist Party leader in Shanghai and member of the elite Politburo, Chen Jining, according to state media.
The 62-year-old, who is the fourth member of the top leadership body to be probed since last year, is suspected of “severe violations of discipline and laws”, the Xinhua news agency reported. The phrase is a common euphemism for corruption.
As part of President Xi Jinping’s widening anticorruption campaign , three Politburo members from the 24-member body have already been removed in its current term, which began in 2022, including General Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission that oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, said Chen’s investigation was part of an “unprecedented pattern”.
“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anticorruption campaign has no limits,” he said.
Chen earned a doctorate in environmental engineering at Imperial College London and rose through the ranks at China’s elite Tsinghua University to become its president.
He entered government as China’s environmental protection minister before becoming the mayor of Beijing. In 2022, he joined the Politburo as the party boss of Shanghai, China’s financial hub.
The post is one of China’s most prestigious provincial-level positions, often serving as a springboard to top leadership roles. Xi briefly served in the role in 2007 before joining the Politburo’s Standing Committee, the country’s highest decision-making body.
China’s second-ranking official, Prime Minister Li Qiang, as well as Vice President Han Zheng, also held the Shanghai post before moving into central leadership roles.
In a separate development, Liu Min, a senior official at the Ministry of Science and Technology, has also been placed under investigation for suspected “serious violations of party discipline and national laws”.

articles.title_orig: Trump appears to make millions from Nvidia intervention over Huang | First Thing
articles.title_zh: Trump appears to make millions from Nvidia intervention over Huang | First Thing
articles.content_orig:
President Donald J. Trump has accomplished something extraordinary. He directly inserted himself into the boardroom of one of America's most strategically important companies, Nvidia , helping to reverse a corporate leadership decision, and personally vouched for restored CEO Jensen Huang as having a clean bill of health regarding the national security investigations into his business activities with China.
On Monday, after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang following his resignation amid a counterintelligence controversy and allegations that Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, is under suspicion of being a Chinese intelligence asset, Wall Street celebrated with a historic market bounce. But the market's enthusiasm should not obscure a far more consequential question circulating in Washington, D.C.: Does American national security have a price?
What happened at Nvidia raises the frightening possibility that it does, and it fits a recent pattern that is exactly what geopolitical rivals around the world want to see. Consider the economic pressures surrounding the Iran war. Disruptions to energy markets, shipping, supply chains, and consumer prices have complicated American strategic decision-making. These are notably different circumstances, but they raise the same troubling question about the costs of defending American national security interests, and when they become economically unpalatable to those in the Trump administration.
Beijing, Tehran, and Moscow are watching — as are our allies and partners — and they all may agree on one thing: America has an Achilles' heel that military and technological superiority cannot overcome. It is possible to impose sufficient economic pain to alter Washington's strategic calculation with friends and foes alike. Bleed American capital markets, disrupt commerce, squeeze consumers, and eventually Washington may look for an exit.
Despite the narrative that the president is weaving, there is a fundamental difference between responsibly weighing economic consequences and allowing adversaries to conclude that they can impose an economic veto over U.S. national security policy. Trump told CNBC in an extensive interview on Monday morning that when it comes to national security, "losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen ... would be a far bigger threat than anything we're talking about."
"The bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was you know he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about, including me, that nobody else understands," Trump said. "This was a big loss. This was a tremendous loss. And you saw that it affected the market. It affected even, I think it even affected the perception of our country in the world," the president said.
And that's true, but not only in the way Trump thinks it did.
This is not about whether Huang is a brilliant executive or whether Nvidia is enormously important to American competitiveness. Both are true. The question that America, particularly its government, must ask is whether Huang's economic importance justifies subordinating corporate governance, interfering with counterintelligence procedures, and stymying national security oversight.
Trump characterized the Justice Department's assessment as having exonerated Huang. Yet Nvidia's board reinstated him while its own review remained open.
The allegations involving reported contacts with Chinese intelligence assets do not establish legal wrongdoing. However, presidential personal assurances are not substitutes for independent counterintelligence assessments and investigations or congressional oversight. Monday's rising stock price might only measure what shareholders believe Huang at the helm of Nvidia is worth, while discounting or ignoring the unresolved counterintelligence risk that Huang may still pose to Nvidia and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem.
The Trump administration, Silicon Valley, and Wall Street may believe the matter is closed.
"That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market," Trump told CNBC about Nvidia's 31.5% Monday gains.
One glaring vulnerability still on the horizon is what Washington does not know. If Beijing possesses additional damaging information, it controls whether, when, and how that information might be weaponized in an ongoing and now reignited strategic competition between the U.S. and China. Beijing retains the capacity to reopen this matter at a time of its choosing. Chinese intelligence could drip-feed disclosures, compel repeated explanations from Huang and the president, and transform Monday's declaration of resolution of this matter into a prolonged national security vulnerability.
There is also a striking irony here. Some pundits are comparing Trump's intervention to China's state-controlled market. To be sure, the Chinese government has a very heavy hand in its economy, but one thing the Chinese Communist Party will never do is put an individual ahead of national security and political authority despite the economic impact that this person or company is perceived to have. Xi Jinping and China's Communist Party have demonstrated a willingness to make almost the opposite calculation about national security and economic growth. Under Xi, national and political security generally takes precedence over the interests of individual companies and brilliant executives.
Consider Jack Ma. In 2020, Beijing halted Ant Group's planned $37 billion initial public offering and subsequently imposed sweeping regulatory restrictions on Ma's business empire. Beijing accepted substantial economic consequences to reinforce national security and political authority. This is not an argument for importing China's authoritarian model into American corporate governance. But the strategic asymmetry is noteworthy to revisit in this latest comparative context. Beijing has demonstrated that even its most celebrated entrepreneurs are not indispensable to the party and the nation. Washington risks signaling that some of its entrepreneurs are in fact indispensable to the state, which ironically potentially makes them even bigger intelligence targets for foreign adversaries.
As an economic matter, the commercial realities of Nvidia's China business make this situation even more perplexing. China, including Hong Kong, accounted for just 9.1% of Nvidia's reported global revenue in fiscal 2026, down from 19.2% the previous year. Its latest fourth-quarter guidance assumes no Chinese data center compute revenue. Nvidia did change the way it reports geographic sales, to customer headquarter address, in late 2025. But anyone familiar with Chinese strategic documents, including the 15th Five-Year Plan, should understand that Beijing has no intention of becoming permanently "addicted" to American chips. Its objective is technological self-reliance, not expanding Nvidia's market share and by extension its dependency on them.
Whatever the exact figure, I cannot think of a number that is worth selling out U.S. national security over, but it certainly isn't  9.1%, which is also a number that will continue to shrink. Furthermore, if the AI ecosystem is critical to our economy and our national security, then selling advanced chips to China or loosening export controls is the opposite of what we should be doing because the chips are used to juice the compute of Chinese LLMs that compete with ours, and to increase the effectiveness and lethality of Chinese weapons systems. The questionable sales of Nvidia chips in Asia, which are at the heart of this story, support neither our economy nor our national security. They undermine them both.
There is also an extraordinary corporate governance precedent that extends well beyond Nvidia and Huang, one that is escalating and growing more bold at each turn. While Trump has intervened in the markets before, in cases including U.S. Steel and Intel , he ha

articles.content_orig:
By TOM COTTERILL, DEPUTY DEFENCE AND FOREIGN AFFAIRS EDITOR and WILL STEWART
Published: 05:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 07:39 EST, 24 November 2026
Vladimir Putin 's bloodbath in Ukraine may have cost the lives of more than 700,000 Russian soldiers, a staggering new estimate has claimed.
The data, based on hacked Kremlin statistics, represents a dramatic escalation from earlier assessments by Western officials, who said 500,000 Kremlin troops had been slaughtered.
If true, Russia's losses would almost eclipse those suffered by both the US and UK combined during the Second World War , which are just shy of 800,000.
It means Putin's military would have suffered one death every three-and-a-half minutes since the despot launched his full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The Kremlin fiercely guards its death toll, but a trove of Russian state data obtained by pro-Ukrainian hackers may now have provided a fresh insight into the consequences of Moscow 's 'meatgrinder' tactics.
Russia's official death toll counts 5,937 soldiers as having been killed in the Ukraine war, although this has not been updated since September 2022 .
Independent Russian investigative outlets Meduza and Mediazona siphoned data from Russia's state statistics service, Rosstat, and found 490,000 military deaths recorded.
However, deaths can take a long time to report, with bodies often left to rot on the battlefield for months, leading to a lag in published figures.
The charred remains of destroyed Russian tanks and armoured vehicles litter the streets of Bucha in March 2022
A Russian T-80BV tank is destroyed during a strike by Ukrainian armed forces
Researchers used statistical modelling to estimate the additional fatalities, with calculations suggesting Moscow could have lost potentially up to 720,000 troops.
Western defence sources have disputed the figures, telling the Daily Mail it appears too high.
The New York Times, which first reported the analysis, also claimed it had not independently verified the researchers' calculations.
The impact on Russian society could be far larger, with the estimates only looking at fatalities and not those injured. It's understood Russia's overall casualty count is now approaching 1.6million.
In the past two months alone, Ukraine has inflicted back-to-back record-breaking casualties on Russian troops.
According to Kyiv, the number of troops killed or injured in October was 54,400 – the highest on record since Putin launched his war.
The scale of Ukrainian military deaths remains unclear, with estimates varying significantly. However, it's widely accepted Russia has likely suffered more casualties than Ukraine.
This is due, in part, to the repeated botched attempts to seize territory through waves of meatgrinder-style assaults and because attacking forces often suffer higher casualties than defending troops, fighting from entrenched positions.
Ukrainian soldiers open a body bag containing the remains of a fallen Russian soldier
Despite the death toll, Putin still appears to show no sign of wanting peace and has launched a series of punishing missile and drone strikes across Ukraine in recent days.
In an appalling new attack on civilians, a Russian bombardment hit an ordinary apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, killing at least two and wounding 40.
Among the victims were four injured children, including an infant.
'A private residential building has been destroyed, and a five-story building partially destroyed,' said Ukrainian official Mykhailo Semikin.
'Multi-story and private houses, cars, and a transportation infrastructure facility have been damaged.
'There is information about people who are trapped. Rescue workers are conducting search and rescue operations.'
Ukraine destroyed a Russian military base for the Rubicon unit in occupied Berdyansk, triggering the explosion of ammunition.
In Moscow, more than 50 passenger aircraft were diverted and dozens of flights delayed as Ukrainian drone threats disrupted Moscow's airports overnight, according to the Russian authorities.

articles.title_orig: Russia accuses NATO member Estonia of hostile actions ‘on the verge of unleashing open war’
articles.title_zh: Russia accuses NATO member Estonia of hostile actions ‘on the verge of unleashing open war’
articles.content_orig:
Russia's Foreign Ministry has lashed out at Estonia's government, accusing the NATO member of carrying out a range of "hostile actions" and putting the Baltic state "on the verge of unleashing open war" with Moscow.
The outburst underscores rising tensions between Russia and countries on NATO's eastern flank and comes after Estonia announced it will close its road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1.
Russia's ministry said Monday it had lodged a formal protest to Estonia's chargé d'affaires, Marek Uhtegi, over Tallinn's decision to close its border crossings and accused the European Union member of imposing a naval blockade against Moscow.
"The Estonian diplomat was again informed that such provocative and extremely dangerous actions are on the verge of unleashing open war with Russia," the ministry said in a statement, describing measures taken by Estonian lawmakers as "Russophobic."
The ministry also accused Estonia of "tacitly" providing its airspace for Ukrainian drone flights and sharply criticized Tallinn's ban on the transit of Russian and Belarusian grain through Estonian territory, referring to a policy that was introduced at the start of October.
Estonia, which shares a 294-kilometer (183-mile) border with Russia, swiftly denied ever allowing its territory to be used for military operations by another country.
It also responded to Russia's allegations by saying the Kremlin appears to be seeking to divert attention from its own efforts to undermine European security.
"Russian missiles have reached Polish territory, Danish security services have identified an assassination plot in Denmark orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, merchant vessels in the Black Sea are under constant threat from Russian attacks, and in Estonia, an arson attack targeting a defence industry company, planned on the orders of Russian military intelligence, was foiled," Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said Monday.
"All this is happening while Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine," he added.
The rhetoric marks a significant escalation in tensions between Estonia and Russia. Tallinn, a staunch Ukraine ally, has frequently raised the alarm over sabotage attacks against NATO countries that have been supporting Kyiv since Russia launched the full-scale invasion of its neighbor in February 2022.
Earlier this month, Estonia said it would close road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1 as it blames Moscow for an attempted "sabotage" of one of its defense companies, an allegation the Kremlin denies.
Tallinn has said the border closure will help to reduce Moscow's ability to conduct hostile activities against it and mitigate risks related to sanctions circumvention.
Ukraine has stepped up its attacks on Russian critical targets in recent weeks, damaging Russian President Vladimir Putin 's prized Crimea bridge , striking a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea and destroying one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port .
The suspected Ukrainian attack on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday prompted Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the Ukraine war is "spilling over" into its immediate vicinity.
Finland, one of NATO's newest members , has also closed its land border crossings with Russia.
Ukraine's latest attacks on some of Russia's most protected targets have demonstrated Kyiv's capabilities to hurt Moscow even without ample U.S. military support, according to Mario Bikarski, senior Europe and Central Asia analyst for Verisk Maplecroft, a political risk consultancy.
"Ukraine will continue to look for ways to degrade not only Russia's economy, but also its geostrategic interests in the wider region, including the Mediterranean and the Middle East," Bikarski said.
The prospect of an imminent peace deal between Russia and Ukraine appears to be slim, Bikarski said, although "the latest surge in diplomatic activity and mounting losses for both sides signals an appetite from all sides to reach an agreement."

articles.title_orig: 'A page out of the Chinese playbook,' How Trump's Nvidia intervention mirrors similar moves by China's government
articles.title_zh: 'A page out of the Chinese playbook,' How Trump's Nvidia intervention mirrors similar moves by China's government
articles.content_orig:
By JON MICHAEL RAASCH, WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT
Published: 10:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 06:09 EST, 24 November 2026
President Donald Trump has revealed what he told Jensen Huang right before the Nvidia chief executive was reinstated, following a 'spy' sex scandal that had forced him to resign.
'I talked to him [Jensen Huang] last night,' Trump told CNBC in an interview. 'I said, 'Jensen, just promise me one thing: You're going to work hard.
'You got brain, you got everything going. You're going to work hard, and if you work hard, there's nobody can beat you'.'
Nvidia's board of directors announced on Monday that the recently ousted boss would return to his position at the helm of the AI giant.
It prompted a stunning rally in Nvidia's shares – adding more than 30 per cent or nearly $1trillion (£763billion) to its value.
'The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,' Trump wrote on social media.
The White House confirmed that Trump called in to the company's board of directors to advocate for Huang's return to leadership.
Huang's whirlwind firing and rehiring after multiple reported affairs, two with Nvidia subordinates and another with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang, have prompted a tumultuous few weeks for the AI firm and the US economy .
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring
Huang's whirlwind firing and rehiring after multiple reported affairs - two with Nvidia subordinates and another with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang - have prompted a tumultuous few weeks for the AI firm and US economy
Trump posted a meme on his Truth Social showing Huang holding up a red bra in a wild re-imagining of the iconic photo after Trump was shot by a would-be assassin in 2023
'He's apologized for indiscretion, which was unfortunate. That was probably that's what brought it to such a level, because sex sells fellas!' Trump said in a CNBC interview Monday morning.
'Now, [Jim] Cramer would not know that because he's a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.'
Trump also claimed that Huang's wife, Lori, 64, has also decided to stand by her husband despite his infidelity.
'He's got a very, very, very good wife, and they've worked it out,' Trump told The New York Times. 'She's a fantastic woman.'
The president separately posted a meme on his Truth Social showing Huang holding up a red bra in a wild re-imagining of the iconic photo after Trump was shot by a would-be assassin in 2023.
Huang met his wife of 41 years at Oregon State University, when they were paired as lab partners in an electrical engineering class. He was 17 at the time.
The couple had already welcomed their two children, Madison and Spencer, by the time he co-founded Nvidia in 1993.
Both Madison and Spencer now hold key positions within high-priority business units at the company.
Lori is the president of the family's $9 billion charitable foundation and often accompanies her husband to events.
As the US's predominant AI company and microchip manufacturer, Nvidia has ballooned to become one of the most expensive US companies and a leader of cutting-edge computational development in the race against China for tech supremacy.
The recent string of damaging stories about Huang's personal conduct contributed to the company hemorrhaging over $1 trillion in market cap.
But the stock roared back to life, gaining over 25 percent on Monday following Trump's announcement that the company is not a national security risk.
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring.
'The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.
Alice Huang pictured with recently reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
Lori Huang and Jensen Huang attend the 12th Breakthrough Prize Ceremony at the Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, April 18, 2026
'The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.'
Huang is still the subject of an internal Nvidia investigation into his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data firm Megaspeed, which has been of particular concern within the administration.
There are suspicions that Alice Huang used her role at Megaspeed to convince the Nvidia boss to allow the sale of advanced chips to the Singapore-based firm before those same chips were used by Chinese AI firms, helping them effectively circumvent an export ban.
US officials noted that the Megaspeed executive speaks English well and has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry
'NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,' Trump said.
Nvidia said in its announcement on Monday that the probe into the 'foreign intelligence effort' will proceed and that the CEO 'fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.'
Additionally, the Nvidia boss is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1 about the affair with the suspected spy.
The company has since established a national security and export control committee to identify possible compliance and security risks.
Trump has grown close with the Nvidia boss during his second term, repeatedly hosting Huang at the White House for ritzy state dinners and inviting him on state visits to China and the United Kingdom.
The president has also traded millions worth of Nvidia stock.
The Republican has made at least 108 transactions worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million during his second term, according to a CNBC analysis of the president's Nvidia stock trades.
His official filing puts his Nvidia holdings at anywhere between $12.5million to $58million (£10million to £45million) at the end of 2025. The White House always says independent managers run Mr Trump's portfolio.
Huang returned Monday to Nvidia headquarters in Silicon Valley, and employees gathered in the building's atrium loudly cheered him on.
'I am going to be a better CEO the second time around,' Huang said.
The CEO, who will also serve as Nvidia president, said in a statement that he was 'honored' to return to the company and that he resumes the responsibility 'with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.'
He thanked board Chairman Harvey C Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress, who will return to her role as chief financial officer, as well as Nvidia's executive staff for their leadership during the brief period of disorder.
'I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,' Huang´s statement said.
'Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can´t wait to get back to work.'
Fox News host Jesse Watters warned Trump that he will face massive Democratic backlash – and maybe even an impeachment attempt – after he saved the embattled Nvidia CEO.
'The Democrats are now licking their chops over the Jensen affair and Trump personally restoring [him] as CEO, even if it was to help the economy and the country,' the commentator said, noting: 'This gives [them] a lot of ammunition.'
'The Democrats will likely use the scandal to impeach,' he then warned.

articles.title_zh: Stock futures decline as Nvidia pulls back, giving back part of Monday’s rally: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO , CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday.
"It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the " Mad Money " host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now."
Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.
"Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary."
Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.
"If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said.
Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.
Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The New York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.
"There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said.
"These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target."

articles.title_orig: Beyond Competition: How China's Automotive Transformation Is Creating New Global Opportunities
articles.title_zh: Beyond Competition: How China's Automotive Transformation Is Creating New Global Opportunities
articles.content_orig:
China's automotive transformation is creating a new set of industrial capabilities that could benefit the global automotive industry as a whole.
Over the past decade, China has developed a highly interconnected automotive ecosystem, bringing together battery technology, intelligent driving, vehicle software, advanced manufacturing, and an increasingly sophisticated supply chain.
The significance of this transformation lies not only in the competitiveness of Chinese automakers, but also in the opportunities these capabilities create for companies around the world.
Volkswagen offers an interesting example. The group is targeting annual exports of around 300,000 vehicles from China by 2030. More importantly, it plans to introduce China-developed vehicle platforms and electronic architecture into selected overseas markets，which represents a meaningful evolution in the role of China within multinational automakers' global operations.
Image source: Volkswagen Group China
For decades, international automotive companies brought technology, manufacturing expertise, management practices, and engineering capabilities to China. These contributions played an important role in the development of China's automotive industry.
Today, we are beginning to see industrial capabilities flow in the other direction as well.
Chinese companies are expanding their manufacturing, engineering, and supply-chain operations overseas. Meanwhile, multinational companies are increasingly integrating China's innovation resources into their global development strategies.
This is not simply a reversal of traditional globalization. It is an evolution toward a more interconnected model of industrial collaboration.
Different markets still have their own strengths. China's rapidly evolving technology ecosystem can complement Europe's engineering expertise, Japan's manufacturing and quality management capabilities, and the growing industrial capacity of emerging markets.
The opportunity is not to replicate the Chinese automotive model everywhere, but to combine complementary capabilities and develop solutions that meet different local needs.
Of course, this transformation brings challenges. Companies must navigate regulatory differences, cultural expectations, financial pressures, and increasingly complex localization requirements.
These challenges also highlight the importance of deeper industrial collaboration, local capability building, and disciplined long-term investment.
For global automotive executives, the strategic question should therefore extend beyond how to compete with Chinese companies. It should also be about how to leverage China's industrial capabilities, integrate them with existing strengths, and create better products and sustainable businesses for consumers around the world .
In my view, the greatest value of China's automotive transformation will not be measured solely by the number of vehicles Chinese companies sell globally. It will also be measured by how much this transformation contributes to the evolution of the entire global automotive industry.
That is a much greater opportunity than winning a car war.

articles.title_zh: China works to suppress India's rise across multiple fronts - USCC
articles.content_orig:
China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.
On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India .
China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report said.
It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.

articles.title_orig: Afghan women with UK university offers 'heartbroken' after visas stopped
articles.title_zh: Afghan women with UK university offers 'heartbroken' after visas stopped
articles.content_orig:
Saurav Das said that he was supposed to deliver a series of lectures in the UK
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.
Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".
It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.
Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests , said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.
He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.
"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," he wrote on X.
A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.
Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.
"The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country," she wrote.
Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.
In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .
In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands of people detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.
The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.
There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.
In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.
In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

articles.title_orig: Trump Administration Imposes Sanctions on Megaspeed, Singaporean Firm at Center of Nvidia Scandal
articles.title_zh: Trump Administration Imposes Sanctions on Megaspeed, Singaporean Firm at Center of Nvidia Scandal
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration on Monday added the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors.
The Singapore-based company was added to the Commerce Departmentâs entity list on Monday afternoon, plans that were first reported by Semafor.
The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
According to a filing from Commerceâs Bureau of Industry and Security posted to the Federal Register Monday afternoon, seven total entities were added to the list from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including various affiliates of Megaspeed, MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. âThese additions are being made because of the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users,â the filing reads. âThese entities will be added with a license requirement for all items subject to the [Export Administration Regulations] and licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial.â
Technology exports already en route to the targeted companies will be allowed to go through, the filing suggests.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been under pressure to place Megaspeed on the departmentâs entity list from others inside the administration, tensions that became public after news broke of Huangâs relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
Earlier this month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency along with the Pentagon, the State Department, and the US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list âfor monthsâ but that âCommerce holds the pen.â Bipartisan lawmakers have pressed Lutnick to put Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls.
âThe Commerce Department placed Megaspeed on the Entity List. This makes it unlawful to export any US-origin goods, software, or technology to Megaspeed,â BIS spokesman Thomas Wackman told Semafor. âIt is also now unlawful to export advanced SI chips to Megaspeed, even if the chips are produced outside the United States. Commerce will continue to vigorously enforce export controls, including these new Entity Listings.â

articles.title_orig: Mayanot Jerusalem Honors Its Partners at Rooftop Celebration
articles.title_zh: Mayanot Jerusalem Honors Its Partners at Rooftop Celebration
articles.content_orig:
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot rooftop has become a Jerusalem landmark, with its breathtaking view of the city, and stunning sunsets. Sitting at the entrance to the city, a stone’s throw from the Machane Yehuda market, and right across from Kraft Stadium, the Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies always has its lights on and is filled with students and teachers learning at all hours of the day.
Recently, we gathered on the rooftop to honor those who helped build and create the Institute, with live music by the Solomon Brothers, and an evening dedicated to our partners and friends. We welcomed David and Eda Schottenstein , who dedicated Mayanot’s beautiful lobby; Abe and Nily Edynast , who donated the main tzedakah box; and Yitzchak Yoel and Roberta Schoen , who dedicated the library in the Beit Midrash.
Rabbi Kasriel Shemtov , Director of Mayanot, introduced Mr. Yitzchak Yoel Schoen for the dedication of the Beit Midrash library, and emphasized, “Torah is something we take with us even when we leave the walls of this yeshiva, and Mayanot endeavors to give students the tools to learn on their own so Torah learning becomes part of their life journey.”
Reb Yitzchak Yoel shared, “The real joy comes not from a plaque like this, but seeing the people use the books daily, and that’s what [Mayanot] is all about.”
David Schottenstein added that those who give to Mayanot are giving “to a place that wants to give to others. You’re building homes, you’re building Jewish homes.”
Friends and family from all 30 years of Mayanot came from around the globe to celebrate. Ken Schuckman , who studied at Mayanot in 1997, came with his sons and said, “Mayanot is probably one of the most popular places in the world! They are still my rabbis and my brothers. And now, look at this. It’s absolutely magnificent. I feel so blessed and proud to be here tonight.”
Israeli Channel 14 journalist, Yedidya Meir , said, “What’s beautiful is not the roof; it’s what happens under the roof.”  That is exactly what Mayanot is: a home for learning and growth, and for following the Rebbe’s mission of spreading light.
Eli S., a lone soldier serving in a combat unit who lives in the Mayanot dorms, said, “I came, and it was the greatest decision I’ve ever made. When I am on base, I can’t wait to get out and come home to Mayanot because it’s such an incredible environment here. This is the greatest way one who wants can contribute to lone soldiers.”
Rabbi Shlomo Gestetner , Dean of Mayanot, spoke about how every single Jew can become someone who learns Torah on a regular basis, and we have the honor and privilege of starting many journeys here at Mayanot.
We are looking forward to many more celebrations here in Jerusalem, at Mayanot, both on the rooftop and within our halls.
